name: French House
about: French house, the French Touch, came out of Paris in the mid-1990s when a generation raised on disco, Chicago house and hip-hop sampling started filtering old records into new ones. Daft Punk's Homework and Discovery made it the most influential dance music of its decade, but the sound was already there in Motorbass, Étienne de Crécy's Super Discount and Dimitri from Paris. Its signature is the filtered loop: a disco or funk phrase swept open with a low-pass filter, a bass guitar bump, a compressed, pumping kick. Cassius, Bob Sinclar, Alan Braxe and Fred Falke carried it to the charts; Justice, Breakbot and Myd kept Paris in the conversation. It remains the city's defining pop export.

artists.name: Daft Punk
artists.why: the robots who exported it worldwide

artists.name: Dimitri from Paris
artists.why: disco scholar of the first wave

artists.name: Alan Braxe
artists.why: co-wrote Music Sounds Better with You

artists.name: Fred Falke
artists.why: the bass guitar in the room

albums.title: Boulevard
albums.why: Ludovic Navarre's F Communications debut folded jazz, dub and deep house into the first French house album with a sound of its own.

albums.title: Pansoul
albums.why: Philippe Zdar and Étienne de Crécy's only album as Motorbass is the French Touch's founding document, hip-hop-raised deep house with a dusty swing.

albums.title: Super Discount
albums.why: De Crécy and friends under budget-sticker artwork made the filtered disco loop a genre, with Prix Choc as its anthem.

albums.title: Sacrebleu
albums.why: A disco scholar's debut, light on its feet, with lounge, bossa and Parisian cliché played as affectionate house; Une Very Stylish Fille remains a classic.

albums.title: Homework
albums.why: Chicago house, acid and filtered disco rebuilt in a Paris bedroom, with Da Funk and Around the World; the record that made the French Touch a world event.

albums.title: Picnic Attack
albums.why: Versatile's first full-length is the stranger, dubbier side of Paris house, with Disco Cubizm as the scene's early anthem.

albums.title: Paradise
albums.why: Christophe Le Friant's Yellow Productions debut, built on Gym Tonic and My Only Love, is French house as glossy, filtered disco pop.
Zdar and Boombass follow Pansoul with a louder, poppier filtered-disco record; Cassius 1999 and Feeling for You are the hits, the rest holds up.

albums.title: Darkdancer
albums.why: Stuart Price posing as a Frenchman made a filter-house and 1980s synth-pop hybrid that anticipated his later Madonna work.

albums.title: Analog Worms Attack
albums.why: Quentin Dupieux's debut is the French Touch's abrasive cousin, with Flat Beat and a puppet; funk reduced to buzzing low end.

albums.title: Installation Sonore
albums.why: Montpellier's guitar-led take on the French Touch, filtered house with real riffs, and La Guitaristic House Organisation as its calling card.

albums.title: Tourist
albums.why: Blue Note signed the French house act that played jazz, and Tourist sold millions on Rose Rouge and Sure Thing without cheapening either side.

albums.title: Discovery
albums.why: Filter house turned into pop, with One More Time, Digital Love and Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger; its influence on the next twenty years is hard to overstate.

albums.title: Modjo
albums.why: Lady took the filtered Chic loop to number one across Europe, and the album around it is better-written than one-hit status suggests.

albums.title: Midnight Funk
albums.why: Jérémie Mondon's debut is late-period French Touch at its most tasteful, filtered funk with the grit still on it.

albums.title: Au Rêve
albums.why: The duo's third album drifts toward soul and hip-hop with real singers, less dancefloor than 1999 but a warmer, more musical record.

albums.title: Super Discount 2
albums.why: The sequel keeps the filtered loops and adds a harder, electro-leaning edge; not the shock of the original, but consistent.

albums.title: The Upper Cuts
albums.why: Braxe, Fred Falke and Kris Menace's singles gathered in one place: the Roulé-school filter house refined into bass-guitar-driven pop.

albums.title: Lucky Boy
albums.why: The late Ed Banger producer's album sits between hip-hop and French house, with I Am Somebody and Signatune as its touchstones.
Distorted, compressed and built from chopped disco, the Ed Banger duo's debut is the French Touch's second coming, with D.A.N.C.E. and Phantom.

albums.title: Sexuality
albums.why: Produced by Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, Tellier's languid synth-pop record is the French Touch's bedroom album and his best.

albums.title: By Your Side
albums.why: Thibaut Berland's Ed Banger debut revives the disco side of French house with live bass and Irfane's falsetto; Baby I'm Yours is the keeper.

albums.title: Umami
albums.why: Lyon's Folamour brought sample-based disco house back as a warm, soulful album, the French Touch for a new generation of record diggers.

albums.title: Born a Loser
albums.why: The Club Cheval member's Ed Banger debut is loose, funny and song-based, French house with the filter dialled down and the guitars up.
